root_cause.text: In `ksmbd`’s `smb2_get_ea()` EA response builder, the code did not recheck `buf_free_len` before writing 4-byte alignment padding with `memset()`, so it could write 1–3 bytes past the end of the shared response buffer after the EA value exactly consumed the remaining space.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (buf_free_len < alignment_bytes) break;` immediately before the unconditional `memset(ptr, '\0', alignment_bytes);`, and the CVE text states the bounds check was done before the value `memcpy()` but the alignment `memset()` “fires unconditionally afterward with no check on remaining space,” causing an out-of-bounds write.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check in smb2_get_ea() to stop writing alignment padding when the output buffer does not have enough free space.
intent_record.what: In smb2_get_ea(), a new conditional check was added before zero-padding for 4-byte alignment: if buf_free_len is smaller than alignment_bytes, the loop breaks instead of calling memset() and advancing the output pointer.
intent_record.how: This prevents writing alignment padding beyond the remaining space in the response buffer, avoiding buffer overrun or corruption when there is not enough room to align the next xattr entry.

grouping_result.intent: Add a bounds check in smb2_get_ea() to stop writing alignment padding when the output buffer does not have enough free space.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds a bounds check in smb2_get_ea() to prevent writing 4-byte alignment padding when the shared response buffer has no remaining space, which is exactly the out-of-bounds write described.

candidates.rationale: This is the unchecked write that pads the EA response to a 4-byte boundary. If the EA value exactly exhausted the remaining buffer space, this memset could write 1–3 bytes past the end of the shared response buffer because no free-space recheck was performed before padding.

This calculation determines how many padding bytes will be written. The vulnerability arises when this padding is computed and then blindly emitted without verifying that buf_free_len still covers it.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the out-of-bounds padding write in smb2_get_ea(). It writes 1–3 alignment bytes after the EA value without rechecking that buf_free_len still has space, which matches the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in this function. After computing the EA payload size, the code aligns the next entry with padding: `alignment_bytes = ((next_offset + 3) & ~3) - next_offset;` and then unconditionally writes the padding with `memset(ptr, '\0', alignment_bytes);` at lines 4287-4293. There is no recheck that `buf_free_len` is still large enough for `alignment_bytes` after the EA value exactly consumes the remaining space. The only bounds check before the write is earlier (`buf_free_len -= value_len; if (buf_free_len < 0) ...`), which does not protect the subsequent padding write. The fix is not present because there is no condition guarding the `memset()` against insufficient remaining buffer space, so this can write 1-3 bytes past the end of the response buffer.
